USMLE-style practice · Orthopedics

monteggia — clinical decision 5

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

Following reduction and fixation of a Monteggia fracture, the radial head looks congruent on one image. The surgeon now checks the elbow through motion before closure. What is the main purpose of this dynamic assessment of the radiocapitellar joint?

  1. Assess distal radioulnar joint stability in isolation
  2. Determine isolated varus-valgus stability of the ulnohumeral joint
  3. Measure postoperative active triceps strength
  4. Evaluate posterior interosseous nerve motor recovery
  5. Confirm that the radial head remains reduced and stable through motion
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Confirm that the radial head remains reduced and stable through motion

A reduced image alone does not prove that the head will remain stable during functional movement.

Understanding the options

Confirm that the radial head remains reduced and stable through motion
A reduced image alone does not prove that the head will remain stable during functional movement.
Assess distal radioulnar joint stability in isolation
The stated assessment observes the proximal radiocapitellar relationship.
Determine isolated varus-valgus stability of the ulnohumeral joint
Collateral stability is a distinct assessment from tracking radial head reduction through motion.
Measure postoperative active triceps strength
Intraoperative passive motion does not measure voluntary triceps power.
Evaluate posterior interosseous nerve motor recovery
Motor function requires a separate neurological assessment; joint congruity does not establish nerve recovery.
